title: Bounded-formula decidability in Heyting arithmetic

based_on.title: From Constructive Mathematics to Computable Analysis via the Realizability Interpretation (doctoral thesis)
based_on.pages: §1.3.2 printed p.25, HA definition only; elementary internal developments supplied locally

summary: Construct native HA decisions and stability for bounded formulas, including nested variable bounds, with explicit expansion, finite search and parameter substitution.
abstract: An assertion that checks every number below a variable bound cannot be proved by writing out one fixed list of numerical cases. Heyting arithmetic can instead prove its finite-search alternatives uniformly in the bound. We use that internal search to construct decision disjunctions for arithmetic formulas whose quantifiers all have arithmetic bounds, including bounds depending on earlier quantified inputs. Each expression is expanded into the original language with zero, successor, addition and multiplication, and every result is an actual intuitionistic arithmetic certificate with fixed finite parameters. Empty intervals, successor endpoints and capture-free term instances are included. The resulting stability proofs are distinguished from numeralwise truth tests, coded PA proof builders and further negative-translation conservation claims.
